column10: A Great White Shark is a large, strong fish that lives in the ocean. It is known for its long, powerful body that can be up to 21 feet–as long as a van! It often lives alone and travels from place to place seeking food like seals, dolphins, fish, or other sharks. It can have around 300 sharp, triangle pointed teeth that can keep growing in if any come out! Like most sharks, Great White sharks can not live in fresh water rivers, ponds, or lakes. They prefer to live in warm salt water oceans near the coastlines of places like South Africa, California, Australia, and New Zealand. Great White Sharks do not have hard bones, instead their skeletons are made of strong, flexible cartilage. Still, scientists have found fossils of their teeth that date back to around six million years ago.
